item.title: Gaywood man’s football magazine shortlisted for national award
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Gaywood man’s football magazine shortlisted for national award
A West Ham United fanzine edited by a Gaywood resident has been shortlisted for a national honour. Blowing Bubbles, edited by TV journalist David Blackmore, is in the running for Fanzine of the Year at the 2026 Football Supporters’ Association Awards. This marks the fourth time the publication has reached the shortlist.
The winner will be announced at a ceremony in London on Monday, November 30. West Ham supporters have until midday on Monday, November 16, to cast their votes for the magazine. The publication, which launched in 2012, has now produced 173 editions, offering fans a platform to share their views on the club.

item.title: South Lynn man sentenced following nightclub incident
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
South Lynn man sentenced following nightclub incident
A 31-year-old man from South Lynn has been sentenced after being removed from a King’s Lynn nightclub. Arturas Cimolonskas of Fisheries Walk was ejected from Bar 100 on Norfolk Street during the early hours of Sunday, October 17, following reports of aggressive behaviour and intoxication.
Police issued a dispersal notice, but Mr Cimolonskas was subsequently arrested for being drunk and disorderly after failing to provide his details. Appearing at Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, he admitted the offence, claiming he only wished to re-enter the venue to retrieve a bag. Magistrates handed him a six-month conditional discharge and ordered him to pay £71 in costs and surcharges.

item.title: West Norfolk Council reveals major parking and regeneration strategy for King’s Lynn
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
West Norfolk Council reveals major parking and regeneration strategy for King’s Lynn
West Norfolk Council has unveiled a new strategy that could see several car parks in King’s Lynn replaced by housing, businesses, and public spaces. Under the proposals, the Tuesday Market Place would see its parking capacity reduced from 210 to 25 spaces to create a pedestrian-focused area. To compensate, the council is considering a new 517-space facility at the town’s port.
The plan aims to consolidate smaller car parks into larger, more efficient sites to support town centre regeneration. Officials have stated that the strategy is designed to maintain overall parking capacity rather than reduce it. The council is now moving forward with a £50,000 feasibility study before presenting final recommendations to the Cabinet.

Wisbech’s Luxe Cinema reopens today
The Luxe Cinema on Alexandra Road in Wisbech is welcoming customers back this afternoon. The venue had been closed since earlier this week due to what management described as unexpected circumstances.
In a social media update posted this morning, a spokesperson confirmed that the cinema is now ready to resume screenings. The closure was necessary while the business renegotiated its insurance policy, a process that has now been resolved. Doors are scheduled to open from 1pm today.

item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
North Lynn man sentenced for assaulting parents
A 40-year-old man from North Lynn has avoided a prison sentence after pleading guilty to assaulting his elderly parents. Peter Goff, of Loke Road, attacked his parents at their home in Great Dunham on April 21 following a night out.
At Lynn Magistrates’ Court on Thursday, Goff received an 18-month community order, which includes 200 hours of unpaid work and a six-month alcohol monitoring tag. He has also been issued a two-year restraining order preventing him from contacting his parents. In addition to the community order, Goff was ordered to pay a £114 victim surcharge and £45 in court costs.
